data.gender_notes: Gudula is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old High German word 'gudal', meaning 'god'. The name Gudula is a feminine form of the name Gudulf, which also means 'God-granting'. In Christianity, Gudula is the name of a virgin and martyr, who is the patron saint of Cologne, Germany. The name Gudula carries the meaning “Power of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Gudula usually hope their child will grow to embody power of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Gudula belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Power of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gudula total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gudula has a rich cultural history in Germany, particularly in Cologne, where she is the patron saint. Her feast day is celebrated with grand processions and festivities every year, attracting thousands of pilgrims. The Cologne Cathedral, one of the city's most iconic landmarks, is dedicated to her, and her relics are kept there.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Gudula represents the deep spiritual connection and devotion that the people of Cologne have with the Christian faith. It is a reminder of their trust in God's protection and the belief that divine intervention can bring about blessings and miracles. The name Gudula also symbolizes the power of prayer and the importance of seeking the intercession of saints in times of need.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gudula is believed to represent the protective power of the Holy Virgin Mary against evil forces. Her name, derived from the Old High German words 'gut' (good) and 'hild' (battle), symbolizes the triumph of good over evil, with the Virgin Mary as the ultimate source of strength and guidance.
